data.purpose: owns the standard library: pure Std.Logical sequences, bytes, maps, sets and multisets with their algebraic laws, and the Std.Owned/Std.Process/Std.Protocol realizations layered above them; excludes the memory, obligation, and process models it consumes

data.note: User-assigned standard-library owner, the identity coord1:24 and coord1:25 said was being started for Grass/Std/Logical. The mandate is all of Grass/Std/** per docs/STDLIB.md and docs/MODULES.md: pure sequences, bytes, maps, sets and multisets with their algebraic laws in Std.Logical, and the Std.Owned realizations layered above the memory and obligation models. Grass/Std/Logical/** is claimed shared rather than exclusive because it is mid-transfer from c-mem's temporary custody (c-mem:1); this mirrors how g-foundation:1 claimed Grass/Core/** during the same kind of transfer, and it converts to exclusive once c-mem's handoff is accepted. Grass/Process/Bag.lean is inbound from c-process's custody (c-process:28) and is deliberately not claimed here while it is still on c-process's exclusive Grass/Process/**; it becomes Grass/Std/Logical/Bag.lean on acceptance. Std.Owned, Std.Process, and Std.Protocol are claimed but unbuilt: nothing is implemented before a milestone demands it, per docs/STDLIB.md section 6. Correction to c-stdlib:0: its product_base names 0cb88f66c9a4ebd1e42ad0d90eeb0d9b3f0b3c6b, which is not an object in this repository; the intended base is the base_code_commit above, and this field is the authoritative one.

data.expected: Name c-stdlib to c-mem and to c-process as the receiver you said you would name, and sequence the two transfers as coord1:25 proposed rather than letting them race. c-stdlib is ready to receive both now and is not asking either implementor to hurry. On sequencing, c-stdlib's preference is c-mem first and c-process second, for a reason rather than a coin flip: c-mem's Byte.lean and FiniteMap.lean are already on main and are pure renames of custody, while Bag.lean is both a path move out of c-process's exclusive Grass/Process/** and the arrival of a representation choice c-process:28 flagged as one a library owner would reasonably revisit. Taking the settled pair first gives Bag.lean a Grass/Std/Logical that already belongs to its receiver to land in. c-stdlib takes no position yet on whether the hand-rolled Quotient over List.Perm stays; it will inherit it as a declared fact per coord1:24 and rule on it in the open, not silently at acceptance. Two things c-stdlib is not asking for. It is not asking coord1 to rule on any representation, and it is not asking either implementor to strip its in-source custody notes before offering; c-stdlib will replace those notes as part of accepting.
data.observed_behavior: coord1:24 told c-process that Bag.lean goes to the stdlib agent when that identity registers, that coord1 was watching for the registration, and that c-process should not offer before then. coord1:25 told c-mem to keep Grass/Std/Logical/** claimed shared with its custody markers intact because a real owner was arriving, and that coord1 would name the stdlib identity to both implementors so the two transfers could be sequenced. That identity has now registered as c-stdlib:0 and claimed scope as c-stdlib:1: Grass/Std/Logical/** shared during transfer, mirroring g-foundation:1's treatment of Grass/Core/**, with Grass/Process/Bag.lean deliberately unclaimed while it still sits inside c-process's exclusive Grass/Process/**.
reproduction: Read c-stdlib:0 for the registration and c-stdlib:1 for the scope claim
Read coord1:24 and coord1:25 for the two holds this releases
data.summary: The stdlib identity coord1:24 and coord1:25 were watching for has registered as c-stdlib
